q6.answer: Order is the coordinator: it moves a checkout forward by reacting to HTTP replies from Inventory and events from Payment, and the Order sweeper repeats stalled steps. The record of progress is the status field on the order row in Order's own database (PENDING_STOCK, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAID_CLAIMING, CONFIRMED and so on), with status_changed_at.

q7.answer: The provider sends a signed webhook to Payment, which checks the HMAC signature and finds the payment by the order id echoed in the reference field. Payment updates its status in P4 and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentFailed through its outbox to the broker, and Order consumes it. A reconciliation job in Payment can also ask the provider if no webhook arrives.

q8.answer: P4 writes the provider event id to a unique-keyed processed_webhook_events table in the same transaction as the status change, so a repeat collides and is ignored with a 200. The payment status is also changed only if it is still REQUESTED. Downstream, Order acts on events only by its current status, so repeated events are ignored.

q9.answer: Payment publishes PaymentFailed, Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderFailed, and Inventory (I4) releases the hold: for each line reserved is reduced and the status becomes RELEASED, but only if the reservation is still RESERVED. If it already lapsed or was released, nothing happens, so reserved is never subtracted twice.

q10.answer: Order asks Inventory to claim by HTTP, and Inventory decides in one transaction. If the hold is still RESERVED it claims. If it is EXPIRED but every line still has enough available stock, it retakes the stock and claims. Otherwise it replies out of stock, and Order cancels as CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer and publishes RefundRequested for a full refund. The retake branch is my own addition.

q11.answer: The refund row was saved as PENDING before the provider was called, so it stays PENDING (a failed or timed-out attempt counts as rejected). The refund scheduler loop in Payment retries it with backoff and the same refund key. After N failures the row becomes REFUND_FAILED and ops is alerted, but retries continue and the row is never dropped until REFUNDED. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table.

q12.answer: Order confirmation causes it. After the claim succeeds Order sets CONFIRMED and publishes OrderConfirmed. The Cart service consumes it and, in one transaction guarded by applied_orders, removes the ordered lines (not the whole cart, which is my decision to confirm). The cart is untouched on any failure.
